name: lorikeet-staffing
description: Forecasts when a support team runs short of agents as tickets grow, and finds the hours of the week with nobody on shift.

interface.longDescription: Plan support headcount with two calculators. The hiring forecast shows when a support team runs short of agents as ticket volume grows, allowing for attrition, hiring lead time and ramp up, and how many people to hire and when to start. The coverage gap check maps when customers contact support against when agents are on shift across time zones, and shows the hours with nobody on, the tickets at risk and what that costs. Same maths as the Hiring Forecaster and Coverage Gap Mapper on lorikeet.tools. What you enter is not saved.
capabilities: See when your support team runs short as tickets grow, and how many people to hire and when.
Find the hours customers contact you with nobody on shift, and what those gaps cost.
defaultPrompt: We have 12 support agents and 9,000 tickets a month, growing 8% a month. When do we need to start hiring?
How many support agents will we need over the next year? 20 agents today, 15,000 tickets a month, growing 5% a month.
Our support team works 9 to 5 in Sydney but most customers are in the US and Europe. Where are our coverage gaps?

positive.prompt: We have 12 support agents and 9,000 tickets a month, growing 8% a month. When do we need to start hiring?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls staffing_forecast. Card titled "Support hiring forecast" with a risk pill, extra agents needed by a month, "Team runs short", "Start hiring" and an "Agents needed vs your team" chart.

positive.description: How many support agents will we need over the next year? 20 agents today, 15,...
positive.prompt: How many support agents will we need over the next year? 20 agents today, 15,000 tickets a month, growing 5% a month.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls staffing_forecast. Same card; the reply names the defaults it relied on (attrition, lead time, ramp up).

positive.description: Our support team works 9 to 5 in Sydney but most customers are in the US and...
positive.prompt: Our support team works 9 to 5 in Sydney but most customers are in the US and Europe. Where are our coverage gaps?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls staffing_coverage_gap. Card titled "Support coverage gaps" with "% covered", tickets at risk a week, the yearly cost of gaps and a half hourly demand chart in UTC marking hours with no one on shift.

positive.description: We have 6 agents in London, 8am to 5pm on weekdays. Which hours have nobody o...
positive.prompt: We have 6 agents in London, 8am to 5pm on weekdays. Which hours have nobody on shift for customers in the Americas, and what does that cost us?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls staffing_coverage_gap with a London shift and Americas demand. Same card, with the gap hours in the evening and weekend.

positive.prompt: Forecast our support hiring: 30 agents, 25% annual attrition, a 3 month hiring lead time and 20,000 tickets a month.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls staffing_forecast with the given attrition and lead time. Card shows agents lost to attrition a year and when to start hiring.
